question: Can the single connected shifted-Y 61-defect component be compressed exactly by a truth-blind within-component separator state space or, if that fails, by a frozen affine-signature quotient, with a polynomial-size proof-carrying relation and reconstruction obligation?

ordered_candidates.name: MIN_FILL_SEPARATOR_STATE_DOOR
ordered_candidates.graph: primal graph on target-component variables; two variables adjacent iff they co-occur in a target defect clause; the single affine equation is tracked as an independent parity side-constraint and is not used to choose the order
ordered_candidates.ordering: deterministic min-fill; tie break by current degree then variable id
ordered_candidates.induced_width: maximum later-neighbor count during elimination after fill edges
ordered_candidates.budget: L^4 where L is literal count of the full effective AW residual
ordered_candidates.accept_if: 2^w <= L^4 and the relation certificate independently verifies all bags, fill edges, clause ownership, parity side-constraint scope, and witness reconstruction map

ordered_candidates.name: AFFINE_SIGNATURE_QUOTIENT_FALLBACK
ordered_candidates.equivalence: variables may share a quotient class only if they have identical signed incidence signatures across all 61 target defects AND identical coefficient in the target affine equation
ordered_candidates.quotient_state_bound: 2^q where q is the number of quotient classes
ordered_candidates.accept_if: 2^q <= L^4 and a proof-carrying relation independently verifies class signatures, exact clause lifting, parity lifting, and model reconstruction to original target variables

frozen_domain.primary: exact AW first component obstruction residual only
